summary: cro checked in 1 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary:
CRO handoff: retain the following as deferred CEO/CTO research leads; do not dispatch, install dependencies, deploy, spend, add telemetry, or change monetization this cycle. Fleet containment remains appropriate because 36 improvements await measurement, 9 implementation requests failed, ownership and validation gates remain incomplete, and only 3 outcomes are proven.

1. Microsoft MarkItDown (MIT): offline conversion of approved internal documents into Markdown could reduce source-backed SEO/content production effort across editorial and affiliate sites. Evidence: weekly trend signal at 187,397 stars; CRO lab passed 8/8 bounded checks with 194 files and no dependency installation. Risks: parser fidelity, transitive dependency and supply-chain review, maintenance, and rights to source documents. Metric: publishable-content throughput, editor correction rate, and indexed-page outcomes; revenue remains unknown. Time-to-learn: 1–2 weeks. Smallest reversible prototype: convert one fixed, owner-approved document fixture in a disposable workspace and compare output against a manually prepared Markdown baseline.

2. Mermaid (MIT): render explanatory diagrams for guides, comparison pages, and technical editorial content where visual structure may improve comprehension and engagement. Evidence: daily trend signal at 90,456 stars; CRO lab supported the SEO-content fit, but no safe native checks were available without installing dependencies. Risks: dependency and rendering security review, accessibility of generated SVG, visual accuracy, maintenance, and no evidence of conversion lift. Metric: assisted-page engagement and search performance using existing telemetry only; causal lift remains unknown. Time-to-learn: 1–2 weeks. Smallest reversible prototype: render one static diagram from a fixed internal fixture offline, then run accessibility and deterministic output checks.

3. shadcn/ui (MIT): selectively adapt accessible, customizable components for repeatable CTA, comparison-card, and merchandising layouts across the fleet, reducing one-off UI work. Evidence: daily trend signal at 124,749 stars; CRO lab completed 3/3 bounded checks across 3 checks, with no dependency installation. Risks: component dependency and provenance review, styling regressions, accessibility validation, bundle impact, maintenance, and cross-site design drift. Metric: preview validation pass rate, task cycle time, Core Web Vitals, and existing CTA/conversion telemetry where available; no lift is assumed. Time-to-learn: 1 week. Smallest reversible prototype: reproduce one page-local CTA component in an isolated worktree without adding it to production or changing shared infrastructure.

4. Affiliate attribution repair as a product opportunity: standardize registered tracking-ID validation and link-level reconciliation before any further affiliate optimization. Evidence: Amazon reports 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission for 2026-09-21; named site rows exist, but the aggregate earnings row is not assignable to a site. Existing site-specific repairs and the pending amputeenews.com tag prerequisite are already in the queue and must not be duplicated. Risks: owner-controlled tag dependency, incorrect attribution, provider-policy constraints, and incomplete matching-period cost evidence. Metric: valid tracking-ID coverage and attributable ordered/shipped items and commission; ROI and margin remain unknown. Time-to-learn: one reporting cycle after existing repairs clear. Smallest reversible prototype: offline validation of registered tracking IDs against generated affiliate URLs and existing configuration, with no credential or production change.
